vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: unhuman
Version: 1.0.1

The skill is classified as suspicious due to its reliance on `npx` for executing external commands, which fetches and runs code from npm, introducing a supply chain risk. It also explicitly instructs the agent to perform autonomous financial transactions via `npx @moneydevkit/agent-wallet send <invoice>`, a high-risk capability, even though it aligns with the stated purpose of domain registration and payment. While no direct malicious intent (like data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints or persistence mechanisms) is evident, the powerful capabilities and inherent risks associated with executing external, remotely fetched code warrant caution.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions match its declared purpose (domain registration + bitcoin payments) but rely on running npm packages via npx and enable fully autonomous bitcoin payments and local token storage without declaring or explaining wallet credentials—this combination is disproportionate and risky.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, commands, and stated behavior align: this is a CLI wrapper for unhuman.domains with optional agent-wallet auto-pay. The requested operations (search/register/manage DNS/renew) match the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent to run npx commands (npx unhuman and npx @moneydevkit/agent-wallet), store management tokens at ~/.unhuman/tokens.json, and perform autonomous payment flows when --wallet is used. The actions are within domain-management scope, but they include autonomous payments and persistent credential storage which broaden the agent's authority.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec, but the SKILL.md relies on npx to fetch and execute packages from npm at runtime. Running npx executes remote JavaScript from the npm registry (unverified code) and will also fetch @moneydevkit/agent-wallet; no provenance, checksum, or publisher info is provided. This is a material risk compared to an instruction-only skill that doesn't execute remote code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, yet it expects an agent-wallet daemon capable of spending bitcoin. Autonomous payment capability can result in real monetary transfers; the skill does not document what wallet credentials or limits are required or used. It also writes management tokens to ~/.unhuman/tokens.json, which is sensitive local state. The lack of declared/proportional credential handling is concerning.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists tokens to the user's home and can start/use a long-running agent-wallet daemon. While it does not request always: true, combining autonomous invocation with the ability to make payments and store tokens increases blast radius—especially without documented safeguards or spending limits.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill behaves like a CLI that will download and run npm packages on demand and can autonomously pay bitcoin invoices using an agent-wallet. Before installing or using it: 1) Verify the npm package(s) (unhuman and @moneydevkit/agent-wallet) and their maintainers on the public registry and review source code if possible. 2) Do not point an agent with real wallet keys or large balances at this skill without setting strict spending limits or using a dedicated, funded test wallet. 3) Be aware it will write management tokens to ~/.unhuman/tokens.json—inspect and protect that file. 4) Prefer running the CLI in a sandboxed environment or container if you must test it. 5) If you need autonomy, require explicit confirmation or limits from the user before any payment action. If you cannot inspect the referenced npm packages or control the wallet, treat the skill as high-risk and avoid giving it access to funds or sensitive credentials.
